For Valves designed for flow in one direction o@y and so marked on the valve the pressure shall be applied on the upstream side of the valve only. In all cases the valve shall open to atmosphere for detection be in the closed of leakage. position with the side not under pressure

For valves in double block and bleed application and for valves with independent double seating, the pressure shall be applied inside the bonnet or body with the discs closed and both sides open' for inspection. Plug and ball-valves shall be operated from filly closed to fully open position three times to demonstrate satisfactory mechenical operation and continued tightness after operation. it is permitted to charge sealant before testing on valves relying on sealing compound to effect seal. 3.4 Nydrostatic Seat Test

3.4.1 The seat test ihall be made with seat clean and free of oil. However, if necessary to prevent galling, the seats may be coated with a film of oil of viscosity not greater than that of This requirement does not apply to a valve in which a lubricant provides the primary kerosene. seal. The seat test shall be carried out by closing the valve in the normal man.ner. 3.4.2 Valve shall be subjected to hydrostatic seat tests at a gauge pressure not less than 110 percent (the hydrostatic seat test pressure shall not exceed the body rating or seat rating whichever is lower) of the rated pressure at 38'C rounded off to the next higher 1 bar increment, This -&all be applied as specified in the seat test (air). There shall be no visible leakage during the test, 3.4.3 For check valves the hydrostatic seat pressure shall be applied on the down stream side. In addition to this, check valves shall also bs tested on the down stream si'de to 25 percent of the lhydrostatic seat test pressure. No leakage is permissible during these tests. 2

Fluid

a) Hydrostatic tests shall be carried out with water at ambient temperature containing water The use of any other liquid is subject to agreement sotuble oil or suitable rust inhibitor. between the manufacturer and the purchaser, and the viscosity of the same shall in no case be greater than that of water. b) The fluid for pneumatic tests shall from oil as much as possible. be either air or inert gas.
